# Sparse quaternary PP codes with binary check weight eight

This self-contained proof package contains two cyclic reversing-PP examples.

| Input | Exact parameters | Check max | Column max | Achieved regular-frame width |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `pp512_128_11_check8/code.json` | [[512,128,11]] | 8 | 4 | 16 |
| `pp1024_256_12_check8/code.json` | [[1024,256,12]] | 8 | 4 | 15 |

These are modest-distance tradeoffs, not claims of optimality. The sparse search
is incomplete. Frame widths are achieved upper bounds and are not proved minimal.
The inputs have seven nonzero entries per quaternary check row. The actual binary
matrices, rather than a coefficient-count estimate, establish the check cap.

Run with Python 3.10+ and a C++17 compiler:

```
python3 check.py
python3 check.py --replay
```

The second command compiles the preserved source into a temporary directory and
freshly repeats both complete exclusions. The package needs no Python libraries.
Executable contents are omitted; replay builds from portable source. Every source/header and physical matrix, plus declared executable fingerprints,
redundant matrix, stdout, and stderr has a SHA256 binding. Empty stderr files are
also bound. `SHA256SUMS.json` checks all package files except itself.

## Construction and coordinates

`C` uses 0,1,2,3 for 0,1,omega,omega² in F4 with omega²+omega+1=0.
`E` contains exponents modulo P, where P=32 or 64. The 3×8 constituent has entries
C_ij t^(E_ij). The second check array reverses t and exchanges the two four-column
halves. The trace basis is (omega,omega²), and binary coordinate (j,b,t) is
(2j+b)P+t. `src/audit_pp.py` independently expands both binary check matrices.
The pivot uses columns 0,1,2; the free columns are 3,7.

Nonzero augmentation of the pivot determinant implies its invertibility in
F4[C_(2^m)], whose augmentation ideal is nilpotent. The code explicitly verifies
the full inverse of g=Delta² and uses it to normalize cofactor seeds. It does not
assume g is a monomial. Each JSON contains Delta, g, its inverse, all four X and
four Z seeds, and an attaining nontrivial logical witness. Reconstruction tests
all translated pairings (the full identity on k logical qubits), the two kernels,
the ranks after adjoining the logical translates, and CSS commutation.

Both inputs have a nontrivial coefficient-cycle holonomy (a displayed 2×2 minor's
diagonal and off-diagonal coefficient products differ), obstructing removal of
all F4 coefficients by constant field row/column rescaling. Their physical Tanner
graphs are connected. These tests are not a classification under arbitrary binary
changes of check basis or all possible notions of decomposition.

## Completed distance exclusions

`exact.stdout` records one unsharded run (`shards=1`, `split_weight=1`) through
weight d-1. All 16 cyclic coordinate-block roots completed. Root r anchors the
smallest occupied binary block at coordinate rP; cyclic translation sends one of
its occupied positions to that anchor. Smaller coordinates are then forbidden.
All possible first syndrome-cancelling branches are searched. The exact engine
also verifies translation invariance of the check and stabilizer rowspaces.

A minimum nontrivial logical can be chosen to be a minimum-weight representative
of its stabilizer coset. It has overlap at most half the weight of each stabilizer
generator, which justifies the coset-leader pruning. If its support contains a
proper zero-syndrome subword, either that subword is nontrivial and lighter, or it
is a stabilizer that can be removed to make a lighter nontrivial word. Thus a
minimum nontrivial logical admits the irreducible-support traversal used by the
engine. The packing tests only prune when disjoint unsatisfied checks require
more remaining support than the weight budget. Candidate witnesses are checked
by exact stabilizer rowspace reduction, rather than a sampled logical test.

The redundant presentation adds the third nonzero F4 trace row (the XOR of the
two basis rows). `check.py` reconstructs this matrix and independently confirms
both equal rowspaces. The physical reflection (j,b,t)->(j+4 mod8,b,-t modP)
exactly exchanges HX and HZ, preserves weight, and maps stabilizers to stabilizers.
Consequently one complete sector exclusion proves the same lower bound in the
other sector. The attaining witness and its reflection supply both upper bounds.

No completed-exclusion claim is made for the other sampled search candidates.

Public receipts have calendar, job, and workstation metadata removed. File hashes
bind the normalized copies. Executable fingerprints are declarations; compiled
binaries are omitted. Portable replay builds from the supplied source.
